walkthroughs.body_html:
Normal blood glucose ≈ 5 mmol/dm³.

After eating, glucose rises. Pancreas releases insulin, telling liver and muscle cells to store glucose as glycogen.

If glucose falls, pancreas releases glucagon, which breaks glycogen back into glucose.

Type 1 — insulin must be injected. Dose depends on carbohydrate eaten.

Example: 1 unit per 10 g carbs. Meal with 60 g carbs needs 6 units.

BMI = mass ÷ height². For 70 kg, 1.75 m: 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 70 ÷ 3.0625 ≈ 22.9.

BMI 25+ is overweight — risk factor for type 2 diabetes.
